name: indian street chicken
instructions:
An indian street-food-style chicken built on a three-powder stack: CURRY POWDER + SHAWARMA SPICE + AMCHUR (dried green mango powder), on chicken thighs, with a VODKA DEGLAZE to lift the fond.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- chicken thighs
- curry powder
- shawarma spice blend
- amchur (mango) powder
- salt
- vodka, for deglazing

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. Season the chicken thighs with salt, curry powder, and shawarma spice.
2. Sear the thighs in a hot pan until browned and cooked through, building fond on the pan.
3. Remove the chicken, then DEGLAZE the pan with a splash of VODKA, scraping up the fond. Let the alcohol cook off and coat the chicken with the pan glaze.
4. Dust with AMCHUR at the end (see the amchur timing note) and serve.
notes:
=== THE SPICE STACK — CURRY POWDER + SHAWARMA + AMCHUR ===

The idea: curry powder and shawarma spice are overlapping warm blends (both carry cumin/coriander/turmeric territory; shawarma adds the cinnamon/allspice/cardamom sweet-warm register), and amchur supplies the fruity tartness that stands in for vinegar — the same acid-dust job it does in the [[pesarattu-wrap]] street-food layer.

=== AMCHUR TIMING — DUST AT THE END ===

Amchur's tartness (citric/malic acid) survives cooking, but the fruity green-mango top notes are volatile and dull out with heat — and the powder can scorch and go bitter in hot dry oil. So it goes on as a FINISHING DUST after the heat, not in the rub. (This placement is a kitchen-theory call, not yet a cook-tested finding — if it turns out it wants to be cooked in, update this.)

=== VODKA DEGLAZE ===

Vodka is the deglazing liquid — neutral spirit, so it lifts the fond and cooks off without adding a wine or beer flavor on top of the already-busy spice stack.
